topic.title: Which third-party pretrained spectrum models are OK? (MS2DeepScore, FIORA, SIRIUS/CSI:FingerID)
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
Following up on the earlier clarification that any weights need the original training code plus permitted training data, could you confirm how this applies to a few commonly used open models and artifacts?

  1. Models trained only on public libraries (GNPS / MassBank / MoNA) with public training code, e.g. MS2DeepScore 2.0 or FIORA-OS: allowed?
  2. SIRIUS / CSI:FingerID: the training set isn't fully public and may include NIST, so I assume not allowed?
  3. Chemical language / graph models pretrained on PubChem structures only (no spectra), used just as a prior over candidates: allowed?
  4. For weights whose training code is public, is it enough to have the code and the permitted data, or does every intermediate file (e.g. a ranker's training table shipped in a public notebook) need to be reproducible bit-for-bit?
  5. PubChemLite (a CC BY 4.0 subset of PubChem) as a candidate source, with attribution: fine?

Thanks, just want to make sure we don't build on something that gets disqualified later.

comments.content:
1. Models trained only on public libraries: correct, allowed
  2. SIRIUS / CSI:FingerID: correct, not allowed
  3. Chemical language / graph models correct, allowed
  4. We need the code that generates the intermediates as well
  5. Yes PubChem Lite is fine
I think a general rule to follow based on the hosts' previous comments is that both training data and training code need to be publicly available under a valid license for it to be eligible.

Follow-up question on one specific case: coleygroup released MIST checkpoints on Zenodo (record 23303289) on Oct 20 under MIT, with the training code public. They are trained on MassSpecGym; the "aug" variant additionally uses simulated spectra from GLACIER-MSG. I assume these are allowed on the same basis as the GLACIER/ICEBERG MassSpecGym weights, but wanted to confirm since the augmented one is partly distilled from another model. Thanks!
